title: Operator-region-assertion middleware, adaptive KMS fallback and audit sampler
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Adds operator-region-assertion middleware, KMS provider selection heuristic, and audit-sampler to reduce retention costs for noisy tenants. Backwards-compatible rollout via feature flag and canary policy.
description:
Motivation: Several enterprise customers require stronger operator scoping and deterministic residency guarantees while minimizing audit storage costs for very high-volume tenants. This PR implements a request middleware that attaches a signed operator-region-assertion (ORA) to operator-initiated requests, an adaptive KMS fallback selector that picks a compatible provider when primary KMS is unavailable or out-of-region, and an audit-sampler that compacts repetitive low-value audit events into compressed summaries.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds ORA middleware (server/edge) which verifies operator session claims, attaches an operator-region assertion header, and vetoes requests that violate service-region bindings.
- Introduces KMS selector with policy weightings: prefers tenant-bound CMKs, falls back to regional shared CMKs, and finally to a cross-region emergency provider with explicit consent flag.
- Implements audit-sampler that observes event frequency per-tenant and emits periodic rollup events plus a bounded stream of original events for high-severity actions.
- Provides feature-flag gated rollout, unit and integration tests, and comprehensive metrics/traces for SLO monitoring.

Checklist:
- [x] ORA header schema and signing/verifying utilities added
- [x] Runtime policy hooks to consult tenancy and region profiles
- [x] KMS fallback decisions logged with explainability tags
- [x] Audit-sampler pluggable by tenant profile, default off for compliance tenants
- [x] E2E tests for residency enforcement and KMS fallback
- [x] Docs and upgrade notes

Design notes: The ORA is a short-lived JWT-like assertion signed by the operator auth service using an operator key. The middleware validates operator identity, extracts the preferred region from the operator claim, and compares against service and tenant region bindings. Failure modes are explicit: soft-deny (reject with guidance) for strict tenants, or attach an advisory header when running in permissive canary. KMS selection is implemented as a deterministic comparator using (1) tenant CMK affinity, (2) region affinity score, (3) provider health/latency. Selection decisions are emitted to the audit stream so they are reconstructible. The sampler uses a hybrid reservoir + time-window compressor to ensure we never drop high-severity events.

ci_summary: All checks passed on merge. Integration test stage initially failed on kms_mock timeout; increased probe timeout and retried. Lint and unit tests passed on first run. Canary smoke tests green in staging.
notes_for_ops: Operators: enable feature flag 'ora_enforce' in small canary region first. Monitor metrics.operator_ora_denies, kms_selector_fallbacks, audit_sampler_rollups. Watch for increase in 4xx errors from clients; use docs/security/kms-fallback-playbook.md for rollback steps.
security_considerations: ORA assertions are short-lived and cryptographically signed; middleware enforces signature and timestamp freshness. KMS fallback logs decisions and is limited by tenant consent profiles. Audit-sampler is disabled for compliance=high tenants to avoid loss of raw events. An internal security review was conducted (ENG-4219).
